current_quantitative_support: C. sinensis DFR is consistently pink-directed across reported stages; C. reticulata and C. japonica have strong red-direction anthocyanin metabolite shifts; oil-Camellia colour material is concordant; Fan2026 same-workbook-crosswalked A rows show 24.7-fold total-anthocyanin heterogeneity within the visible A class
current_gap: common functional ortholog/paralog map and comparable quantitative coverage across additional wild species
macro_role: estimate anthocyanin-state displacement, within-A intensity/composition variation and node reuse on macro transition branches
claim_boundary: do not treat visible A or all KEGG DFR/ANS homologs as one interchangeable molecular state

current_quantitative_support: C. sinensis FLS is stage/paralog heterogeneous; anthocyanin-minus-flavonol is directionally positive in all four currently admitted quantitative independence clusters
current_gap: matched FLS expression/metabolite evidence across more independent wild systems
macro_role: separate flavonol allocation from anthocyanin and PA in latent-state histories
claim_boundary: four-system directional concordance is not a natural transition-frequency estimate

current_quantitative_support: C. sinensis is developmentally mixed for anthocyanin-minus-PA while three other quantitative systems are positive; oil-Camellia PA itself rises from W to R even as anthocyanin rises more strongly
current_gap: matched PA metabolites plus validated LAR/ANR orthology across more systems
macro_role: model PA allocation independently and test co-activation versus trade-off
claim_boundary: do not merge LAR/ANR/PA with FLS/flavonol into one competitor scalar

current_quantitative_support: C. huana supplies an independent within-species colour-variant axis: RS1 vs GS1 has 21/22 differential carotenoids higher in red material and RS2 vs GS2 has 18/18 higher in red; yellow Camellia studies provide additional but heterogeneous chemistry
current_gap: standardized carotenoid abundance and ortholog-level expression across the same phylogenetic species set
macro_role: separate carotenoid-derived yellow/red contribution from flavonoid state and test independent state-vector displacement
claim_boundary: one C. huana system proves dimensional possibility, not a genus-wide red-carotenoid rule; visible yellow is not carotenoid-only

current_quantitative_support: same-red C. japonica and C. rusticana differ in pollinator-relevant spectral/UV signal while quantitative pigment evidence also shows large within-visible-state biochemical variation
current_gap: standardized spectra/UV and optical traits across the same phylogenetic species set
macro_role: map biochemical state vector to pollinator-perceived phenotype and compare against visible hue
claim_boundary: not derivable deterministically from human-visible hue
